gaps.sentence: It was ___ of you to double-check the figures (SENSE).
gaps.explanation: 'It was sensible of you to do something' praises good judgement; 'sensitive' means easily affected.

gaps.sentence: The crowd waited ___ for the gates to open (PATIENT).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'waited': patiently. 'Patients' are people in hospital.

gaps.sentence: Their ___ was celebrated with a big party (MARRY).
gaps.hint: noun needed after 'Their'; note the spelling change
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'marry' is 'marriage' (-age); an adjective cannot follow 'Their' as subject.

gaps.sentence: We ___ the cost of the trip and ran out of money (ESTIMATE).
gaps.hint: judged it too low — that is why the money ran out (under-)
gaps.explanation: Running out of money shows the estimate was too low: underestimated (under- + estimated).

gaps.sentence: Be careful not to ___ the medicine — read the label twice (USE).
gaps.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrongly: misuse means to use something incorrectly. A base verb follows 'not to'.

gaps.sentence: He made a ___ mistake and lost all the data (CARE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -less means without: careless means not taking care. It modifies the noun 'mistake'.

gaps.sentence: In my opinion, that restaurant is ___ — the food is nothing special (RATE).
gaps.explanation: 'Nothing special' shows the restaurant is praised too much: overrated (over- + rated).

gaps.sentence: She has been a loyal ___ (EMPLOY) of the firm for twenty years.
gaps.hint: person needed: someone who works for the firm
gaps.explanation: An employee works for a company; 'employment' is the uncountable state of having a job.
